title: Diodes: direction, drop and stored energy
summary: Read diode polarity and datasheet limits, then place rectification, flyback and light-emitting diodes in their proper roles.

blocks.title: A one-way tendency, not an ideal check valve
blocks.body: A diode strongly favors one current direction, but it has forward loss, reverse leakage, finite switching time and hard limits. Use the check-valve analogy to remember direction, then return to the datasheet.

blocks.heading: 1. Read bias from anode to cathode

columns.name: Forward bias
columns.detail: The anode is more positive than the cathode by enough to support the operating current. Forward voltage is a result at a stated current and temperature, not a universal 0.7 V switch point.

columns.name: Reverse bias
columns.detail: The cathode is more positive than the anode. Only leakage should flow in normal operation, until breakdown or another rating is exceeded.

blocks.heading: 2. Ratings and curves belong together
blocks.body: Start with repetitive reverse-voltage rating, average or continuous forward current, surge current, forward voltage at stated current, leakage, junction-temperature limit and thermal resistance. For switching work, also check reverse-recovery behavior or the relevant charge specification. A headline current rating is valid only under its stated lead, case, board and temperature conditions.

blocks.heading: 3. Match the diode to the job
items: Rectification steers current when converting or protecting supply paths. Verify reverse voltage, current, loss and surge conditions.
A flyback or freewheel path gives an inductive load current somewhere to go at switch turn-off. Clamp choice also affects release time.
An LED converts current to light. It normally needs current limiting; its forward voltage is not a current regulator.
A Zener or avalanche device can clamp near a designed voltage in a specified current range. It must dissipate the resulting energy without exceeding pulse or thermal limits.

blocks.title: Never infer polarity from package shape alone
blocks.body: Bands, flats and lead lengths can help only when the package drawing confirms them. Use the part marking and manufacturer drawing; verify circuit polarity before power is applied.

blocks.heading: 4. Check the model
blocks.prompt: A 24 V output will drive an indicator LED directly because the LED datasheet lists a 2 V forward voltage. What is missing?
options: A current-limiting design and its power check.
Nothing; the LED fixes the current.
blocks.explanation: Forward voltage does not regulate LED current. The remaining voltage must be handled by a suitable current-limiting circuit, and component power must be checked.

items.label: Name the job
items.detail: Write whether the diode is rectifying, clamping, freewheeling, emitting light or serving another role.

items.label: Record the stresses
items.detail: List expected forward current, reverse voltage, switching rate, pulse energy and ambient or case temperature.

items.label: Find the conditions
items.detail: For every copied rating, also copy the test or thermal condition.

items.label: Check orientation
items.detail: Mark anode and cathode from the manufacturer package drawing, not memory.
